assertion_results.text: Step 0 extracts the Embargo policy URL from the Security Configuration as an optional field without raising an error (§1.71 — backward compatible extraction)
assertion_results.evidence: In data-extraction.md, the 'Configuration Extracted (Step 0)' table includes 'Embargo policy URL | https://example.com/security/embargo-policy'. The field was extracted successfully as part of Step 0 configuration extraction without any error or warning, consistent with optional-field handling.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 evaluates the CVE severity — CVSS 7.5 (High) meets the Critical/Important threshold (CVSS >= 7.0) and triggers the embargo warning gate (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: In embargo-check.md, the Severity Evaluation table explicitly states: CVSS Score 7.5, Severity High, Trigger threshold 'Critical or Important (CVSS >= 7.0)', Threshold met 'Yes (7.5 >= 7.0)'. The warning gate section confirms: 'the CVE severity (High, CVSS 7.5) meets the trigger threshold (CVSS >= 7.0), the following embargo warning gate is presented to the engineer'.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 presents a warning gate to the engineer including the CVE ID (CVE-2026-31812), severity level, a statement about embargo risk, and a link to the configured embargo policy URL (https://example.com/security/embargo-policy) (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: In embargo-check.md, the warning gate block contains all four required elements: (1) CVE ID: 'CVE-2026-31812'; (2) severity level: 'High severity'; (3) embargo risk statement: 'High-severity vulnerabilities may be under embargo. Before proceeding, verify with your security team that this CVE is cleared for public triage.'; (4) embargo policy URL: 'Embargo policy: https://example.com/security/embargo-policy'.

assertion_results.text: Step 1.7 requires explicit engineer confirmation (Yes/No) before proceeding to Step 2 — the gate is a confirmation prompt, not an informational message (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: In embargo-check.md, the warning gate ends with 'Proceed with triage? (Yes / No)' — an explicit confirmation prompt. The Decision Flow section reinforces this: 'The engineer must confirm whether this CVE is cleared for public triage before proceeding to Step 2 (Version Impact Analysis).' It further specifies: 'If Yes: Proceed to Step 2 as normal. If No: Stop execution.' This is a blocking gate, not informational.

assertion_results.text: The embargo warning gate does NOT trigger for Low or Moderate severity CVEs (CVSS < 7.0) — it is skipped silently when severity is below threshold (§1.70)
assertion_results.evidence: The outputs only demonstrate the positive case (CVSS 7.5 triggering the gate). While embargo-check.md defines the threshold as 'CVSS >= 7.0' and shows conditional logic, there is no output or evidence demonstrating that a Low or Moderate CVE (CVSS < 7.0) is handled — no negative test case showing the gate being skipped silently. The threshold logic is stated but never exercised for the below-threshold scenario.
